notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 02/17/2026
Patient: Lance Morar, 72-year-old male

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 02/17/2026. The study demonstrated severe sleep-disordered breathing. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 57.2 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 8% of all events. Sleep architecture was disrupted with frequent arousals related to respiratory events. Oxygen saturation showed intermittent desaturations corresponding to apneas and hypopneas.

In summary, the findings confirm severe sleep apnea with a predominance of obstructive events and a smaller proportion of central and mixed apneas. Clinical correlation and appropriate management are advised.

Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 07/23/2026
Patient: Lance Morar, 72-year-old male

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation of sleep-related concerns and assessment of overall sleep health.

History:
Mr. Morar reports experiencing daytime fatigue and occasional morning headaches. He denies any recent changes in sleep patterns or new medications. No history of restless legs or parasomnias noted.

Physical Examination:
Vital signs are stable. BMI 33.4 kg/m2. No craniofacial abnormalities observed. Neck circumference is within normal limits.

Assessment:
The patient presents with symptoms suggestive of possible sleep-disordered breathing. Given his BMI, he is at increased risk for obstructive sleep apnea.

Plan:
Recommend overnight polysomnography to evaluate for sleep apnea and other sleep disorders. Advise weight management strategies to reduce risk factors. Follow-up after sleep study results to discuss further management options.

Summary:
Mr. Morar is a 72-year-old male with a BMI 33.4 kg/m2 presenting for sleep evaluation. Further diagnostic testing is planned to clarify diagnosis and guide treatment.
